symptom: Control does not start after power-on; the PPU screen stays black
steps: Check the status LED on the PPU panel.
If the status LED is lit: power off, check that the CF card is inserted properly, then power on again and check whether the fault is gone.

If the status LED is off: check the power supply interface X1 on the back of the PPU – loose connection, whether the 24 V terminal matches the interface, and measure the 24 VDC supply with a multimeter.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: HMI screen or the keys on the PPU do not respond
steps: Check whether the control has crashed. If yes, restart the control and check whether the fault still exists.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: MCP does not respond after power-on: all MCP status LEDs are off, or all MCP status LEDs flash continuously
steps: Check that the connection cable between the MCP and the PPU is intact and properly connected; verify by trying a new cable.
Check whether PPU interface X30 or MCP interface X10 is damaged or has bad contact; verify by trying a new cable.
Check the PLC program – a PLC program fault can also make all MCP status LEDs flash.
If the fault still exists, the PPU or MCP is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Some MCP keys do not respond, typically RESET or CYCLE START
steps: Select the system data operating area (SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM).
Open the PLC status window via the softkeys PLC → PLC status.
Monitor DB1000.DBB3: the RESET key is DB1000.DBX3.5 and the CYCLE START key is DB1000.DBX3.3.
If the status bit changes when you press the key, the key works – look for other alarms or check the PLC program elsewhere.
If the status bit does not change when you press the key, the key is damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Spindle does not move, the screen shows it is waiting for the spindle signal, no alarm
steps: Check machine data MD30200 (1 = spindle with encoder, 0 = spindle without encoder).
Analog spindle: check spindle interface X54 on the back of the PPU for looseness or damage, and after starting the spindle measure the voltage output between pins 1 and 9 of X54 with a multimeter.
Check that the connection cables of the PPU, spindle drive and encoder are in good condition.

Check machine data: MD30130 = 1; MD30240 encoder type (1 = motor encoder, 2 = external encoder via X60); MD30134 spindle output polarity (0 = dual polarity, 1/2 = single polarity, as applicable); MD32250 = 100 and MD32260 consistent with the rated motor speed.
Check whether the spindle drive has a fault.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Spindle speed values are shown on the screen but the spindle does not move, no alarm
steps: Check that the control is not in program test state: the program test LED on the MCP must be off and the PRT icon in the PPU program status bar must be deactivated.
If the fault still exists, carry out the checks for spindle fault case 1 (3.5-1): machine data MD30200/MD30130/MD30240/MD30134/MD32250, interface X54, connection cables and the spindle drive.

symptom: Spindle speed is unstable and varies during rotation
steps: Check for interference between connection cables; route power cables and signal cables separately.
Analog spindle: check interface X54 on the back of the PPU for looseness, damage or bad contact.
Check whether the connection cable to the spindle drive is loose or the drive is damaged.

symptom: Spindle does not move and alarm 025000 (hardware fault of active encoder) is shown
alarm_text: Axis MSP1 hardware fault of active encoder
steps: External spindle encoder: check spindle encoder interface X60 on the back of the PPU for looseness or damage.
Check whether the spindle encoder cable is damaged or connected incorrectly.
Check machine data MD30200 (number of encoders: 1 = with encoder, 0 = without) and MD30240 (encoder type: 1 = motor encoder, 2 = external encoder via X60).
Check whether the spindle encoder is damaged: replace it with a new one and test again.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Handwheel does not work or cannot be assigned to an axis
steps: Check that the operating sequence is correct and that the feed axis is selected for handwheel assignment in handwheel mode; use PLC monitoring to test the input/output status of the selected axis traversing key.
Check the handwheel connections and look for short circuits between adjacent connections.
Check interface X10 on the back of the PPU: loose connection, damaged cable, and 5 V output at terminals 5/6.
Check whether the handwheel itself is damaged.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Screen shows the feed axis moving but the axis does not actually move
steps: Check that the control is not in program test state: the program test LED on the MCP must be off and the PRT icon in the PPU program status bar must be deactivated.
Check whether the mechanical coupling is loose.
Check the connections between the control and the drives, and whether the drive terminals are damaged.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Axis moves in the opposite direction to the one selected or shown on the screen
steps: Check machine data MD32100 (axis traversing direction, default 1, change to -1 if required) and MD32110 (encoder position feedback polarity, default 1, change to -1 if required).
SINUMERIK 808D: also check the +DIR and -DIR terminal connections on the drives.

symptom: In JOG mode the axis moves only in one direction and the direction cannot be changed
steps: Check whether the corresponding drive is damaged.

symptom: Positions in the machine coordinate system are inaccurate
steps: Check that machine data match the actual mechanics: MD31030 leadscrew pitch; MD31050/MD31060 denominator/numerator of the gear ratio; MD31020/MD31400 = 10000 encoder lines per revolution (SINUMERIK 808D only) – also check whether there is frequency multiplication on the drive encoder.
Check that the turret is installed properly on the machine.
Check whether the mechanical coupling is loose or the belt is slipping.
Check whether leadscrew pitch compensation and/or backlash compensation need adjusting.

symptom: Tool cannot be changed, the wrong tool is changed, or the turret keeps rotating
steps: Check the phase sequence of the machine power supply / turret motor connection.

Check the turret rotation output / turret in-position input interface on the back of the PPU: damage, loose wires, terminals 1 and 10 connected to 24 V and 0 V respectively, and wiring that matches the PLC program settings.
Check the wires between that interface and the turret for looseness or damage.
Check whether the turret signal encoder on the machine is damaged.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: During tool change the tool arm does not return to its home position
steps: Check the PLC output signals related to the tool arm positions.
Check the PPU input signals related to the tool arm positions.
Note: this can be caused by interference on the turret signals from unstable supply voltage and contactor arcing.

symptom: Axis cannot move or moves with difficulty because of overload; the drive may show an overload alarm
steps: Check that guide lubrication is sufficient: lubricating pipe/nozzle not blocked, lubrication interval not set too long.
Stop the machine and check whether the guides or screws are blocked by machining chips; clean them if needed.
Check that the shaft coupling runs smoothly and is concentric.

symptom: System crashes while starting up; the HMI usually freezes at about 40 %
steps: Power off, restart the control and check whether the fault is resolved.
Power off and check that the CF card is inserted correctly and has no bad contact, then power on again.
If the fault still exists, the PPU is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Hardware limit switch alarm (e.g. 021614) is shown on the PPU
steps: Hold down the RESET key on the PPU while pressing the axis traversing key to move the axis in the opposite direction; the alarm clears once the axis has moved off the hardware limit switch.
If the fault still exists: check the hardware limit switch connection with a multimeter and check whether the limit switches are damaged.

symptom: Axis has passed the hardware limit but still moves without any alarm
steps: Check whether the hardware limit switch wire is short-circuited to the high-level signal.
Check whether the hardware limit switches are damaged.

symptom: During reference point approach the position values on the PPU do not change and the axis does not move
steps: Check whether there is an alarm on the PPU screen; clear it with the RESET key and continue.
If alarms 004060, 004062 and 004065 appear, the machine data has been lost: restore the backup data, power off and restart, then check whether the fault is gone.

symptom: During reference point approach the position values on the PPU change but the axis does not move
steps: Check that the control is not in program test state: the program test LED on the MCP must be off and the PRT icon in the PPU program status bar must be deactivated.
Check machine data: MD30130 = 2, MD30240 = 3, MD30350 = 0.

symptom: During reference point approach the axis keeps moving until the hardware limit switch alarm appears
steps: Check whether the machine deceleration switches or their connections are broken.

symptom: During reference point approach the axis always moves in the opposite direction
steps: Check whether the deceleration switches fail to spring back.
Check for a connection fault of the deceleration switches.

symptom: During reference point approach the axis moves only a short distance
steps: Check machine data MD34000 – the deceleration switches are not used when MD34000 = 0.

symptom: Alarm 20002 appears after the axis leaves the deceleration switch during reference point approach
steps: Check whether the machine approach switch and its connections are damaged.
Check that machine data MD34060 is set properly.
Check whether the feed axis encoder and its connections are damaged.

symptom: JOG and automatic program execution work normally, but nothing happens when approaching the reference point
steps: Check machine data MD30200 – the reference point cannot be approached when MD30200 = 0.

symptom: After reference point approach the axis position is off by one leadscrew pitch
steps: Check that machine data MD31020 is set correctly.
Alternatively, adjust the reference cam switch by 2 to 3 mm.

symptom: Drive alarm; the drive shows A05/A06 (SINAMICS V60) or F30001 (SINAMICS V70): IGBT or internal chip overcurrent
steps: Check the U, V, W and PE connections on the drive: short circuits between phases, a disconnected U/V/W phase, incorrect or poor grounding, damaged wires.
Power on again and check whether the fault still exists.
If it does, check the motor insulation for damage and replace the motor if necessary; power on again and check.
If the fault still exists, the drive is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Drive alarm; the drive shows A07 (SINAMICS V60) or F30002 (SINAMICS V70): ground connection short-circuited
steps: Check the U, V, W and PE connections on the drive for short circuits between phases.
Power on again and check whether the fault still exists.
If the fault still exists, the IGBT module in the drive is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Drive alarm; the drive shows A08: incorrect encoder U/V/W connections
steps: Check the signal cable between the motor and the drive (drive to motor encoder): faulty internal contacts, poor cable shielding, shield ground connected correctly.
Power on again and check whether the fault still exists.
If it does, check the connection of the encoder interface.
If the fault still exists, the motor encoder is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Drive alarm; the drive shows A09 (SINAMICS V60) or F31117 (SINAMICS V70): encoder TTL pulse fault
steps: Check the signal cable between the motor and the drive (drive to motor encoder): correct encoder cable connection, faulty internal contacts, poor cable shielding, shield ground connected correctly.
Power on again and check whether the fault still exists.
If it does, check the connection of the encoder interface.
If the fault still exists, the motor encoder is probably damaged – replacement and maintenance are needed.

symptom: Drive alarm; the drive shows F7452 (following error out of tolerance) or F7011/A7012 (motor overload)
steps: Check whether the cutting load is too high, or whether the spindle stops while the axes are still moving.
Milling machine: check whether the counterbalance for axis Z is too light or its pressure is too low.
Check whether the encoder cable is loose.

section: 3.17 Option activation failure after PPU replacement
symptom: After replacing the PPU, previously purchased options cannot be activated because the old license key is invalid
steps: Recommended: after the first power-up with the new PPU, import the commissioning archive created with the previous PPU.
Contact the Siemens Hotline to unassign the option licenses.
On the PPU: SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM → extended softkeys (>) → Serv. displ. → Version → License key; note the CF card serial number shown in the dialog.

On a PC with internet access, open the Web License Manager (www.siemens.com/automation/license), log in via "Direct access" and assign the purchased licenses to the new PPU; a license key is generated.
Enter the generated license key in the License key dialog and confirm with OK.
Press the Options softkey to check the licensing status, set the licensed options as required, then press NCK reset (po) to restart the NCK.
If the CNC lock function is used, further activation steps are needed (see 3.17-lock-1 / 3.17-lock-2).

section: 3.17 Option activation failure after PPU replacement
symptom: After PPU replacement, a commissioning archive made while CNC lock was deactivated was imported, and CNC lock must be activated again
steps: This is done by the machine manufacturer or dealer: a new activation file (.clc) must be created and imported.
In Access MyMachine on a PC: Tools → CNC lock function... → Activate.

Enter: software version 4.7 SP4; serial number of the new CF card (PPU: SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM → > → Serv. displ. → Version → License key); serial number of the new PPU hardware (from the PPU rating plate); OEM PIN (8–32 characters, mixing upper and lower case letters, numbers and special characters, no spaces); lock date (last or new lock date).
Click Creating LockSet file... to save the .clc file, and store it on a USB stick or connected network drive.
On the PPU open the License key dialog (SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM → > → Serv. displ. → Version → License key) and check that it shows "CNC lock is activated: No lock data".
Press Import File, select the directory with INPUT, select the activation file and confirm with OK.
If no error occurs, CNC lock is active and the lock date is shown on the HMI.

section: 3.17 Option activation failure after PPU replacement
symptom: Alarm 8062 and NC start disabled after PPU replacement, because the imported commissioning archive was made while CNC lock was activated
steps: Cause: the new PPU and new CF card have new serial numbers. The machine manufacturer or dealer must create and import a deactivation file (.clc).
In Access MyMachine on a PC: Tools → CNC lock function... → Deactivate.
Enter: serial number of the new CF card, serial number of the new PPU hardware, and the originally assigned OEM PIN.
Click Creating LockSet file... to save the .clc file, and store it on a USB stick or connected network drive.

On the PPU open the License key dialog (SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM → > → Serv. displ. → Version → License key), press Import File, select the directory with INPUT, select the deactivation file and confirm with OK.
If no error occurs, CNC lock is deactivated. To activate it again, a new activation file is needed (see 3.17-lock-1).

symptom: Alarm 8060 or 8061: the CNC lock .clc file contains incorrect data
steps: Check the alarm cause: cause 13 = .clc file version not supported; cause 14 = CF card serial number not correct; cause 15 = lock date invalid.
Correct the error in the .clc file with Access MyMachine (AMM) and import it again.

symptom: Alarm 8063: reminder showing the remaining days before NC start is locked by CNC lock
steps: Contact the machine manufacturer or dealer to extend or deactivate the CNC lock function.

symptom: Alarm 8064: CNC lock date reached, NC start is disabled
steps: Contact the machine manufacturer or dealer to deactivate the CNC lock function.

symptom: Alarm 8065 after NC restart: a date earlier than the actual date was set, NC start is disabled
steps: Correct the date on the HMI and perform an NC restart again.

symptom: Alarm 8066: the system date was set relative to the CNC lock date in a way that is not allowed
steps: If the date set is equal to or later than the lock date and no NC restart has been done yet: correct the date on the HMI.
If an NC restart has already been done, alarm 8064 is issued and NC start is disabled; the machine manufacturer must deactivate and/or reactivate CNC lock according to its status.
If a future date earlier than the lock date was set and no NC restart has been done yet: correct the date on the HMI.

If an NC restart has already been done, the future date is taken as the actual date and cannot be reset, which shortens the time until the lock date; the machine manufacturer must deactivate and/or reactivate CNC lock according to its status.
Detailed alarm descriptions are in the SINUMERIK 808D Diagnostics Manual.

section: 3.19 OEM PIN forgotten for CNC lock
symptom: The machine manufacturer or dealer has forgotten the OEM PIN for CNC lock and cannot create a valid activation file
steps: The machine manufacturer or dealer contacts the Siemens Hotline and provides: the license certificate (CoL) for the CNC lock option, the CF card serial number, the PPU hardware serial number and the CNC software version (PPU: SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM → > → Serv. displ. → Version).
Import the activation file received from the Hotline into the control to unlock the machine.
Note: this unlocks only the PPU hardware, not the PLC project – the original PLC project for the machine must be available.

symptom: Reminder, not a fault: the handwheel is active and assigned to an axis
steps: No action is required; the alarm disappears when the handwheel is deactivated or unassigned.

symptom: Reminder, not a fault: the spindle is braking
steps: Wait until spindle braking has finished; the alarm then disappears.

symptom: Spindle gear change took longer than the time limit
steps: Check whether the gear change monitoring time is set too short.
Check the spindle gearbox for mechanical problems.

symptom: Control receives no gear level signal or the wrong gear level signal
steps: Use PLC monitoring to check whether there is an input signal at the gear level signal input.
Check whether the input terminals of that interface on the back of the PPU are damaged or loose.
Check the spindle gearbox for mechanical problems.

symptom: Drive is not ready for operation; always appears together with an emergency stop alarm
steps: Check whether an emergency stop alarm is active on the control, which causes this alarm.
Check whether the drive has an alarm, is not started, or is damaged.
SINAMICS V60 drive: also check terminal X6 for loose or broken wires and faults at pins 65 and M24.

symptom: Coolant motor is overloaded and the coolant function does not work
steps: Check whether the overload protection switch of the coolant motor works.
Check interface X102 on the back of the PPU: pin 7 connection loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Lubricating oil level in the oil box is below the minimum; risk of mechanical damage
steps: Check whether the lubricating oil level is too low and add lubricating oil promptly.
Check the relevant interfaces on the back of the PPU: input terminals damaged or loose, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Reminder, not a fault: the first preset maintenance task is due soon
alarm_text: Warning: the 1st maintenance task will expire
steps: Check the preset service maintenance plan and make the necessary preparations.
Select the system data operating area (SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM).
Press the > key for the extended softkeys.
Open the service planning screen with the Serv. planr. softkey.
Press the Task completed softkey to cancel the alarm.

symptom: The first preset maintenance task is now due and must be carried out immediately
alarm_text: Alarm: the 1st maintenance task has expired
steps: Select the system data operating area (SHIFT + SYSTEM ALARM).
Press the > key for the extended softkeys.
Open the service planning screen with the Serv. planr. softkey.
After carrying out the service plan, press the Task completed softkey to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Program test state cannot be changed while a program is running; the channel must be reset first
alarm_text: PRT/AFL change not possible: channel not reset
steps: Press ALARM CANCEL on the PPU to cancel the alarm; the program continues.
Alternatively press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm; note that this also resets the program execution.

symptom: Coolant level in the machine is below the minimum; risk of mechanical damage
steps: Check whether the coolant level is too low and add coolant promptly.
Check interface X102 on the back of the PPU: pin 6 connection loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Lubrication motor is overloaded and the lubrication function does not work
steps: Check whether the overload protection switch of the lubrication motor works.
Check the relevant interfaces on the back of the PPU: input terminals damaged or loose, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Tool magazine is detected in neither the spindle position nor the original position; tool change stops
alarm_text: Magazine not in spindle pos. or original pos.
steps: Check interface X101 on the back of the PPU: input state of I1.3/I1.4 via PLC status monitoring, pins 5 and 6 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check whether the switches that detect the magazine's extended and retracted limits are faulty.
After the magazine has returned to the correct position, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Tool magazine is detected in the spindle position and the original position at the same time; tool change stops
alarm_text: Magazine in spindle pos. and original pos.
steps: Check interface X101 on the back of the PPU: input state of I1.3/I1.4 via PLC status monitoring, pins 5 and 6 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check whether the switches that detect the magazine's extended and retracted limits are faulty.
After the magazine has returned to the correct position, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Magazine move key was pressed while the magazine or spindle was not ready; the magazine does not move
alarm_text: Magazine rot. failed: magazine/spindle not ready
steps: Press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.
Note: the magazine cannot move while the spindle is rotating, the magazine is rotating forward/reverse, the spindle is executing a tool release command, or emergency stop is active.

symptom: Tool on the spindle is different from the tool in the program; the program cannot run
alarm_text: Blk search finds tool on spindle <> tool programed
steps: Check that the tool number to be activated in the current program matches the tool currently loaded on the spindle.
Use the correct program search method to restart the program.
After eliminating the fault, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Spindle tool release takes longer than the monitoring time and fails
alarm_text: Spindle positioning to unclamping position timeout
steps: Check interface X101 on the back of the PPU: input state of I1.5 via PLC status monitoring, pin 7 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check that the tool release monitoring timer T19 in the PLC is set correctly.
Check that the air pressure is sufficient.
Check that the spindle tool release switch works normally.
After eliminating the fault, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Spindle tool clamping takes longer than the monitoring time and fails
alarm_text: Spindle positioning to clamping position timeout
steps: Check interface X101 on the back of the PPU: input state of I1.6 via PLC status monitoring, pin 8 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check that the tool clamping monitoring timer T20 in the PLC is set correctly.
Check that the air pressure is sufficient.
Check that the spindle tool clamping switch works normally.
After eliminating the fault, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Part program cannot start because the safety door is not closed
alarm_text: NC start not possible: safety door not closed
steps: Check that the safety door is closed; if a safety door key on the MCP is used, check that it is activated.
Check interface X102 on the back of the PPU: pin 7 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check that the door-closed limit switch works normally.
After eliminating the fault, press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm.

symptom: Chuck is not clamped; cycle start and spindle rotation are blocked
steps: Check that the chuck control key on the MCP is activated (indicator lit).
Check that the workpiece is clamped in the chuck.
Check interface X102 on the back of the PPU: pin 5 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Chuck was operated while the spindle or the part program was running
alarm_text: Chuck operation not allowed: spindle/prog. running
steps: Press ALARM CANCEL on the PPU to cancel the alarm; the program continues.
Alternatively press RESET on the MCP to cancel the alarm; note that this also resets the program execution.

symptom: Turret motor is overloaded; the turret and all operations are unavailable
steps: Check whether the overload protection switch of the turret motor works.
Check interface X102 on the back of the PPU: pin 2 loose or broken, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: Programmed tool position number is larger than the maximum tool position number
alarm_text: Prog. tool pos. number > max. tool pos. number
steps: Check the part program and correct it according to the actual number of tools created.

symptom: Maximum number of tools is set incorrectly on the control (should be 4 or 6)
steps: Check that machine data MD14510[20] (max. tool number) is set correctly.

symptom: No position signals are detected from the turret
alarm_text: No tool position signal from turrent
steps: Check the turret encoder and whether the turret signal interface is damaged.
Check whether the turret has a fault.
Check the corresponding I/O interface on the back of the PPU: connections disconnected or broken, terminals damaged or loose, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.

symptom: No tool position is detected within the time limit during tool change
steps: Check the turret encoder and whether the turret signal interface is damaged.
Check whether the turret has a fault.
Check the corresponding I/O interface on the back of the PPU: connections disconnected or broken, terminals damaged or loose, pin 10 properly connected to 0 V.
Check that machine data MD14510[22] is set correctly; the value can be increased as appropriate.

symptom: Control does not detect the tool clamp signal
steps: Check whether the relevant input terminals on the back of the PPU are loose or damaged.
Check whether the connections of those input terminals are damaged or broken.
Use PLC monitoring to check whether there is a signal at the corresponding input.

symptom: G81 does not work after switching the control to ISO mode
steps: Replace -ZSFR[0] with -ZSFR[10]: the tool change cycle uses -ZSFR[0], which by default conflicts with the ISO machine data.

symptom: In MDA mode M10 does not work and the chuck cannot be clamped
steps: The PLC program contains an interlock that blocks program execution while the chuck is released; the PLC subroutine must be modified.
Typically, with the chuck released, the spindle is not allowed to run CW or CCW in positioning or oscillating mode.

symptom: In AUTO mode M11 does not work and the chuck cannot be released
steps: Program a dwell of at least 2 seconds between M5 and M11, for example: M5 (spindle stop), G4F2 (2 s dwell), M11 (chuck release).

symptom: Internal thread cutting stops before the cycle is finished; no alarm and the spindle keeps running
steps: Check the value format of CYCLE99 parameter APP (run-in path, without sign): a decimal point may have been entered between the two commas for APP.

section: 5.4 Wrong zero offsets in ISO mode
symptom: Zero offset activated in ISO mode cannot be reset to zero after switching back to Siemens mode
steps: Select the Machine operating area.
Switch to MDA mode.
Enter in the block editor: G291 and then G50.3 X0 Z0.
Press CYCLE START on the MCP; the zero offset previously activated in ISO mode is reset to zero.
